label: second copy step (t=L+1) of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at step t = L+1, where the input is the first copied token and the model must output original token 1. For L=3 this happens on every such step (dev precision 1.0, about 99.5% of activation mass), with activations around 0.3-1.0 of max. At L=4 it also fires weakly (<0.1 of max) at the same position on a minority of sequences. Nothing fires in the original or delimiter phases, at any other recall position, or for L >= 5. Token identity changes magnitude only a little: the largest activations come when out_tok/next_out is a, y, d, r, or s (e.g. y a s <DEL> [y] a), and activations are slightly lower when the input token repeats or when the sequence contains digits.

issues: Minor factual inaccuracy: the explanation says L=4 firings are 'under 0.1 of max', but test misses include 'z a d s <DEL> [z:0.16]'. They are still weak and hold only 0.5% of the mass.

Minor: 'never fires at any other recall position' is not strictly true. Dev shows 9 firings at recall_idx==2 and test shows 6, all in L=3 at the last step, around 0.01-0.02 of max, with 0% of the mass. This is spillover noise.

L=4 firings occur on only about 1.8% of L=4 recall_idx==1 steps. Broadening the predicate to (recall_idx==1)&(L<=4) gives recall 0.9996 but precision 0.166, test F1 0.285, so it is worse. The original predicate is the right one.

Core claims check out on the test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.908, F1 0.952, mass recall 0.995. There is no activity in the original or delimiter phases, and none for L>=5. The misses fall in the lowest activation quartile (coverage 0.63 there, 1.0 in the other quartiles). I did not check the token-magnitude claims (a/y/d/r/s); they are secondary.
